newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Utilicorp hits back at PowerNZ delays.
newsitem.headline: Utilicorp hits back at PowerNZ delays.

text.p: Utilicorp New Zealand, controlled by U.S. power company Utilicorp, said on Wednesday it planned to challenge legal moves by Power New Zealand's (PNZ) independent directors that it fears could delay its plans for a joint takeover.
Utilicorp and local company Mercury plan to pool their respective shareholdings in electricity distributor PNZ in order to take shared, 64 percent control through a joint venture.
Although the plan has been cleared by monopolies authorities independent directors of PNZ have started legal action relating to a long-standing cornerstone agreement with Utilicorp.

Utilicorp has said the jv plan will only take effect if the cornerstone relationship is terminated. Both it and Mercury believe that the agreement no longer adds value to PNZ and should be ended. However, Utilicorp has also had legal advice that its venture plan does not breach the agreement, it said.
"PNZ's actions are not in the best interests of the company," Utilicorp added in a statement.
"The delay of the introduction of the sensible business measures which would improve the company's performance for the benefit of all stakeholders is extremely unfortunate," it added.
